He played for 11 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Chicago Bulls]], [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], and [[Orlando Magic]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|University of Connecticut]], where he won a national championship in 2004.{{Cite web |url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/MBasketball/2004/PlayerBios/Gordonbio.html |title=Ben Gordon |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040417033555/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/MBasketball/2004/PlayerBios/Gordonbio.html |archive-date=April 17, 2004 |publisher=UConn Huskies |access-date=July 31, 2006}} Gordon is the only player to have ever won the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]] as a rookie. He is fourth in career three-point field goals for the Chicago Bulls, behind [[Kirk Hinrich]], [[Zach LaVine]], and [[Coby White]].[https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CHI/leaders_career.html Chicago Bulls Career Leaders] URL last accessed April 27, 2009 He shares the NBA record for most three-point field goals in a game without a miss (9) with [[Latrell Sprewell]] and [[Jalen Brunson]]. ==Early life== Gordon was born in London, England, to a Jamaican father and an African-American mother. He moved to the United States as an infant, and grew up in [[Mount Vernon, New York]]. Gordon played high school basketball for the Mount Vernon Knights, and helped lead the team to the 2000 New York State Public and Federation Championships. Gordon was an All-State player at Mount Vernon and a top-40 national recruit. He was heavily recruited by [[Seton Hall University|Seton Hall]], but decided to attend [[University of Connecticut|UConn]]. ==College career== As a [[freshman]] at [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], Gordon ranked second on the team in [[Score (game)|scoring]] (12.6 ppg), despite coming off the bench for most of the season. He hit the game-winning [[three-point shot]] against [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] in the [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]].[http://www.nba.com/draft2004/profiles/BenGordon.html Ben Gordon prospect profile and college stats] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060628160345/http://www.nba.com/draft2004/profiles/BenGordon.html |date=June 28, 2006 }} URL last accessed July 31, 2006 As a [[wiktionary:sophomore|sophomore]] Gordon averaged a team-leading 19.5 points (which ranked 50th in the nation) and also led the Huskies with 156 total [[Assist (basketball)|assist]]s, which earned Gordon Second Team All-Big East honors. In Gordon's junior and final year at UConn, he averaged a team-leading 20.5 points (again ranked 50th in the nation), 4.7 rebounds and 4.5 assists. He also connected on 104 three-pointers, the second-highest single-season total in UConn's history. Gordon set a [[Big East Conference|Big East]] Tournament record with 81 total points, earning the tournaments' Most Outstanding Performer honors. Gordon also earned the Most Outstanding Player award of the [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]] Regional honors in the [[2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. He also led the tournament field with 127 total points, as he helped lead the Huskies to the [[2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA championship]]. Following his junior year, Gordon declared himself eligible for the [[2004 NBA draft]] and was selected third overall by the [[Chicago Bulls]], one pick after the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] drafted his UConn teammate, [[Emeka Okafor]]. ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2004–2009)=== ==== 2004–05 season: Sixth Man of the Year ==== [[File:Ben Gordon.jpg|thumb|Ben Gordon signing autographs before a Chicago Bulls game]] Before the [[2004 NBA draft]], Gordon thought that he would be drafted anywhere from 7th to 12th, but as the draft got closer he claimed to have an inkling that the Bulls might draft him third as they did with [[Michael Jordan]] 20 years earlier in the [[1984 NBA draft]]. "I'm a guy who looks at the significance of numbers a lot. Before the draft, I had no idea I'd get drafted third. I thought I was going to go anywhere from 7th to 12th. As we started getting closer and I started to get an inkling that the Bulls could be a team that I could end up playing for, I started to look at the numbers. Michael Jordan was drafted by the Bulls and he was the third pick just like you."[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/andrew_lawrence/11/10/gordon.interview/ Q&A: Ben Gordon] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080717184427/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/andrew_lawrence/11/10/gordon.interview/ |date=July 17, 2008 }} URL last accessed November 17, 2006 Gordon wore the number 4 on his [[Jersey (clothing)|jersey]] in high school and college, but had to wear the number 7 with the Bulls due to the number 4 being retired. Gordon said, "I wore No. 4 my whole career but, of course, [[Jerry Sloan]] already had that number beforehand so there wasn't much I could do about it. So all I did was just [put together] being the third pick with my old No. 4. That's why I wear No. 7." The Bulls also acquired [[Luol Deng]] in the same draft. Between Michael Jordan's departure in 1998 and Gordon's arrival in 2004, the Bulls did not win more than 30 games in a single season. In his [[2004–05 NBA season|rookie year]], Gordon helped lead a turnaround from a 3–14 start to finish 47–35 and secure the fourth seed in the [[2005 NBA playoffs|playoffs]]. He averaged 15.1 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game while playing 24.2 minutes per game. Gordon also finished with 21 double-digit fourth-quarter-point performances, second to only [[LeBron James]]'s 22 in the NBA.[https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/fource_0405.html Ben Gordon, Chris Duhon, Andres Nocioni and Luol Deng Bulls Fource] URL last accessed August 1, 2006 In their first playoff appearance in the post-Jordan era, the Bulls (without Luol Deng) lost to the [[Washington Wizards]] in six games. After the season, Gordon became the first rookie in league history to be awarded the [[NBA Sixth Man Award]].[http://www.nba.com/news/gordon_050503.html Gordon named NBA's 6th man] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905171440/http://www.nba.com/news/gordon_050503.html |date=September 5, 2008 }} URL last accessed July 31, 2006 Gordon was also the NBA's [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] Rookie of the Month 3 times (January through to March),[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ben_gordon/bio.html Gordon named rookie of the month for January, February, and March] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060830121106/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ben_gordon/bio.html |date=August 30, 2006 }} URL last accessed July 31, 2006 and was also voted onto the NBA All-Rookie First Team. [[File:Ben Gordon1.jpg|left|thumb|upright|Gordon during a [[2008–09 Chicago Bulls season|2008–09 regular season]] game with the Bulls]] Gordon also had problems with turnovers (4.46 per 48 minutes; sixth in the league in 2004–05), however, and an overall lack of stamina in his rookie season. He remarked, "More than anything, I just want to come back [in the fall] in better shape. ... A lot of this game is about conditioning and how long you can give your best performance."[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/gordon_050810.html Bulls.com interview with Ben Gordon] URL last accessed on July 31, 2006 Gordon also revealed that he was in the process of designing an energy drink called BG7, an allusion to his initials and jersey number. Gordon unveiled the drink at One Sixty Blue, a restaurant co-owned by Michael Jordan. The drink was made with [[white tea]],{{cite news |title=Gordon still sippin' pretty: He has his own drink |date=May 18, 2006 |work=Chicago Sun-Times }} which has a very high amount of [[antioxidant]]s, and the most [[Phenolic content in tea|polyphenols]] of any tea. ==== 2005–06 season ==== In his [[2005–06 NBA season|sophomore campaign]], Gordon alternated between the starting lineup and bench for the Bulls, starting 47 games (mostly in the later half of the season) while coming off of the bench for 35. The minutes Gordon played per game rose, as did his scoring and assist averages.[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ben_gordon/index.html?nav=page Stats and Bio] URL last accessed August 1, 2006 Gordon was selected to play for the Sophomores in the [[Rising Stars Challenge|Rookie Challenge]] held during the [[NBA All-Star Weekend]], in which he scored 17 points.[http://www.nba.com/allstar2006/rookie_challenge/ Recap for 2006 Rookie Challenge game] URL last accessed July 31, 2006 On April 14, 2006, in a Bulls win over the Washington Wizards, Gordon tied [[Latrell Sprewell]]'s NBA record for the most three-pointers made in a game without a miss 9.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/260414004|title=Gordon 9-for-9 from 3-point range as Bulls beat Wiz|accessdate=December 16, 2023|date=April 15, 2006|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} The Bulls returned to the playoffs but were again eliminated in the first round in six games; this time they lost to the [[Miami Heat]], who went on to win the NBA championship. ==== 2006–07 season ==== Gordon's [[2006–07 NBA season|third season]] marked a giant step forward for himself and the Bulls. He adjusted to becoming the team's starting shooting guard, averaging 21.4 points on near-46% shooting in 33 minutes per game. Chicago rebounded from a 3–9 start to finish 49–33. On March 4, 2007, Gordon established a career-high 48 points, leading a miraculous comeback effort to win 126–121 in overtime against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].Yahoo! Sports, [https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2007030415 Chicago 126, Milwaukee 121, OT] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070314045218/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2007030415 |date=March 14, 2007 }} URL last accessed March 27, 2006 In the first round of the [[2007 NBA playoffs|playoffs]] the Bulls again faced the Heat, but this time won the series in four games, becoming the first team in NBA history to sweep the defending champions in the first round. They lost to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the second round, but were able to force the series to six games after initially falling behind 3–0. ==== 2007–08 season ==== On the heels of their first playoff series win in nearly a decade, the Bulls entered the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]] with high expectations. Prior to the season, Gordon and Deng both turned down offers for contract extensions, believing they could earn more in free agency.[http://www.nysun.com/sports/lebrons-shadow-looms-over-free-agent-market/81022/ LeBron's Shadow Looms Over Free Agent Market] Following a 9–16 start, [[Scott Skiles]] was fired and the Bulls did not recover. The Bulls drafted [[Derrick Rose]] with their first overall pick in [[2008 NBA draft|2008]], raising questions about how Gordon and Rose could coexist in Chicago's backcourt (both were score-first guards). ==== 2008–09 season ==== On October 1, 2008, Gordon finally accepted a one-year qualifying offer of $6.4 million after being unable to secure the contract that he was hoping for.[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/64248-chicago-bulls-ben-gordon-loses-contract-battle CHICAGO BULLS' BEN GORDON LOSES CONTRACT BATTLE] On December 27, 2008, Gordon passed [[Scottie Pippen]] as the Chicago Bulls' career leader in three-pointers made. As had been the case in his previous four seasons, the Bulls' season got off to a rocky start. However, Gordon and Rose developed chemistry playing with each other, and helped the Bulls finish the season on a 15–8 run to just qualify for the playoffs at 41–41. Entering the [[2009 NBA playoffs|playoffs]] as the seventh seed and matched with the defending champion [[Boston Celtics]], critics and observers expected the Bulls to be swept. However, in a series that featured the scoring exploits of Gordon (42 points in game 2)[https://web.archive.org/web/20170331120257/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290420002 Allen hits winning 3 as Celts overcome Gordon's 42 points to even series] and [[Ray Allen]] (51 points in game 6),[https://www.nba.com/games/20090430/BOSCHI/recap.html Bulls beat Celtics in 3 OTs, force Game 7] seven overtime periods and five games decided by a single basket, the Bulls pushed the series to seven games before finally losing. Gordon led the Bulls in scoring for the season and playoffs, averaging 20.7 and 24.3 points, respectively. ===Detroit Pistons (2009–2012)=== [[File:Gordon7 12042009.jpg|thumb|upright|Gordon spent ===Charlotte Bobcats (2012–2014)=== [[File:Bobcats vs Nets.jpg|thumb|upright|Gordon with the Charlotte Bobcats in 2013]] On June 26, 2012, Gordon and a future first-round pick were traded to the Charlotte Bobcats in a deal that sent [[Corey Maggette]] to the Pistons.{{cite web |last=Phaler |first=S. |date=June 26, 2012 |title=Bobcats Acquire Ben Gordon, Future First-Round Pick From Pistons |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/bobcats-acquire-ben-gordon-future-first-round-pick-pistons |access-date=June 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} On November 28, 2012, Gordon scored 20 points in the fourth quarter of an eventual 91–94 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. The 20 points were the most in one quarter for any player in Bobcats history. He finished with 26 points on 7-of-11 shooting, making 7-of-10 from beyond the arc, to go with 5-of-5 free throws. On March 2, 2014, he was waived by the Bobcats.{{cite web |last=Rochinski |first=Matt |date=March 2, 2014 |title=Cats Request Waivers on Ben Gordon |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/cats-request-waivers-ben-gordon |access-date=June 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} ===Orlando Magic (2014–2015)=== On July 11, 2014, Gordon signed a two-year, $9 million contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite news |last=Savage |first=Dan |date=July 11, 2014 |title=Magic Sign Ben Gordon |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-ben-gordon |access-date=June 26, 2023}}{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234087/Ben-Gordon-Agrees-To-Two-Year-$9M-Contract-With-Magic|title=Ben Gordon Agrees To Two-Year, $9M Contract With Magic|date=July 12, 2014|work=RealGM.com|access-date=July 12, 2014}} Gordon's final NBA game was played on March 22, 2015, in a 100–119 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]]. In his final game, Gordon played for 14 minutes and recorded 3 points, 1 rebound and 1 assist. On June 29, 2015, he was waived by the Magic.{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=June 29, 2015 |title=Magic Waive Ben Gordon |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-ben-gordon |access-date=June 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} ===Golden State Warriors (2015)=== On September 28, 2015, Gordon signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite news |last=Fischer |first=Paige |date=September 28, 2015 |title=Warriors Sign Ben Gordon |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-ben-gordon |access-date=June 26, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 14, after appearing in two preseason games.{{cite news |date=October 14, 2015 |title=Warriors Waive Guard Ben Gordon |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/ben-gordon-waived-20151014 |access-date=June 26, 2023}} ===Texas Legends (2017)=== On January 24, 2017, Gordon was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|title=Legends Acquire Ben Gordon|url=http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-acquire-ben-gordon/|access-date=January 24, 2017|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 24, 2017}} ==National team career== On April 1, 2008, Gordon was named to the shortlist for the [[Great Britain national basketball team|British national basketball team]]. Gordon is eligible for the team by virtue of his British birth and dual citizenship.[http://sports.aol.com/nba/story/_a/chicago-bulls-guard-ben-gordon-called-up/n20080401112009990018 Chicago Bulls guard Ben Gordon called up to British basketball squad]. AP Sports. April 1, 2008. Retrieved April 5, 2008. In 2010, he said he hoped to represent Great Britain in the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Olympics]].[https://www.hoopsfix.com/2010/08/ben-gordon-looking-to-suit-up-for-gb-next-summer/ Ben Gordon Looking to Suit Up for GB Next Summer]. hoopsfix.com. August 28, 2010. Retrieved September 1, 2010. However, Gordon missed the beginning of Great Britain's June 2012 pre-Olympic training camp in [[Houston]], Texas.{{cite news|title=Myles Hesson Called Up, Gordon a No-Show|url=https://www.hoopsfix.com/2012/06/myles-hesson-called-up-gordon-a-no-show/|access-date=June 17, 2012|work=HoopsFix.com|date=June 17, 2012}} He later said he could not commit to the team after being traded from [[Detroit Pistons|Detroit]] to [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte]].{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2012 |title=Ben Gordon decommits for Britain |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/summer/2012/basketball/story/_/id/8118936 |access-date=June 26, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On July 22, 2016, it was announced that Gordon would be selected for Great Britain's 24-man preliminary roster for the [[EuroBasket 2017 qualification|EuroBasket 2017 qualifiers]].[http://www.gbbasketball.com/news/3974.php#.V5I4_7m9LCQ GREAT BRITAIN REVEAL PRELIMINARY 24 FOR EUROBASKET 2017 QUALIFIERS]. gbbasketball.com. July 22, 2016. Retrieved July 22, 2016. Gordon made Great Britain's 12-man roster for the EuroBasket 2017 qualifiers, and during the qualification games, he averaged 9.2 points, 4.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game.[https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/qualifiers/player/Benjamin-Ashenafi-Gordon Ben GORDON #7 GUARD Height: 191CM / 6'3" Nationality: ENG.] Gordon previously represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2003 Pan American Games|2003 Pan American Games]].[http://www.insidehoops.com/usa-basketball-080703.shtml USA Men Lose Bronze Medal Game]. insidehoops.com. August 7, 2003. Retrieved June 18, 2008. ==Post-playing career== On June 1, 2017, Gordon was arrested for pulling fire alarms at his Los Angeles apartment building.{{Cite web |last=Maloney |first=Jack |date=June 2, 2017 |title=Report: Former NBA guard Ben Gordon arrested for ... pulling fire alarms? |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/report-former-nba-guard-ben-gordon-arrested-for-pulling-fire-alarms |access-date=June 26, 2023 |website=cbssports.com}} In October 2017, Gordon was hospitalized for a [[Psychological evaluation|psychiatric evaluation]] after an altercation with a female patron at a holistic wellness center in Mount Vernon, New York.{{cite news|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/ben-gordon-hospital-psychiatric-bulls-mount-vernon/|title=Ben Gordon hospitalized after bizarre incident|work=Chicago Sun-Times|author=Dan Cahill|date=October 26, 2017|access-date=October 26, 2017}} On November 20, 2017, Gordon was arrested again for punching a manager of an apartment complex, pulling a knife on him and robbing him of his security deposit. He was ticketed, released on a $50,000 bail and had to appear in court.{{cite news |date=November 28, 2017 |title=Former NBA player Ben Gordon arrested after incident at apartment complex |publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21600538 |access-date=November 28, 2017}} In February 2020, Gordon revealed he was suffering from [[bipolar disorder]], and detailed his battles with mental illness since retirement in an article about mental health for [[The Players' Tribune]], including a suicide attempt.{{cite web |last1=Gordon |first1=Ben |title=Where Is My Mind? |url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/articles/ben-gordon-mental-health-nba |website=The Players' Tribune |access-date=February 21, 2020 |date=February 21, 2020}} On October 10, 2022, Gordon was arrested for allegedly punching his son at [[LaGuardia Airport]] in New York and subsequently resisting arrest. Gordon's son had an order of protection since 2018, legally barring his father from taking him outside of Illinois and "committing physical abuse, harassment, or the interference with personal liberty".{{cite web |date=October 12, 2022 |title=Former NBA player Ben Gordon charged with assaulting son, police |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/34783224 |accessdate=June 26, 2023 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}} Shortly afterwards, in early December, he was arrested and sent to Harlem hospital after attempting to stab several people with sewing needles.{{Cite web |last=Rawcliffe |first=Tristan |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Ben Gordon detained and sent to Harlem hospital after reportedly trying to stab random people with sewing needles |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/ben-gordon-detained-sent-harlem-hospital-reportedly-trying-stab-random-people-sewing-needles |access-date=August 31, 2024 |website=Sportsskeeda}} On April 4, 2023, Gordon was arrested once again and taken into custody after he had, allegedly, threatened employees of a juice shop with a knife in [[Stamford, Connecticut]].{{cite
